    --> stdlib/builtins.pyi:4344:1

4344 | / @overload
4345 | | def open(
4346 | |     file: FileDescriptorOrPath,
4347 | |     mode: OpenTextMode = "r",
4348 | |     buffering: int = -1,
4349 | |     encoding: str | None = None,
4350 | |     errors: str | None = None,
4351 | |     newline: str | None = None,
4352 | |     closefd: bool = True,
4353 | |     opener: _Opener | None = None,
4354 | | ) -> TextIOWrapper:
4355 | |     """Open file and return a stream.  Raise OSError upon failure.
4356 | |
4357 | |     file is either a text or byte string giving the name (and the path
4358 | |     if the file isn't in the current working directory) of the file to
4359 | |     be opened or an integer file descriptor of the file to be
4360 | |     wrapped.  (If a file descriptor is given, it is closed when the
4361 | |     returned I/O object is closed, unless closefd is set to False.)
4362 | |
4363 | |     mode is an optional string that specifies the mode in which the file
4364 | |     is opened.  It defaults to 'r' which means open for reading in text
4365 | |     mode.  Other common values are 'w' for writing (truncating the file if
4366 | |     it already exists), 'x' for creating and writing to a new file, and
4367 | |     'a' for appending (which on some Unix systems, means that all writes
4368 | |     append to the end of the file regardless of the current seek position).
4369 | |     In text mode, if encoding is not specified the encoding used is platform
4370 | |     dependent: locale.getencoding() is called to get the current locale
4371 | |     encoding.  (For reading and writing raw bytes use binary mode and leave
4372 | |     encoding unspecified.)  The available modes are:
4373 | |
4374 | |     ========= ==========================================================
4375 | |     Character Meaning
4376 | |     --------- ----------------------------------------------------------
4377 | |     'r'       open for reading (default)
4378 | |     'w'       open for writing, truncating the file first
4379 | |     'x'       create a new file and open it for writing
4380 | |     'a'       open for writing, appending to the end of the file if it
4381 | |               exists
4382 | |     'b'       binary mode
4383 | |     't'       text mode (default)
4384 | |     '+'       open a disk file for updating (reading and writing)
4385 | |     ========= ==========================================================
4386 | |
4387 | |     The default mode is 'rt' (open for reading text).  For binary random
4388 | |     access, the mode 'w+b' opens and truncates the file to 0 bytes, while
4389 | |     'r+b' opens the file without truncation.  The 'x' mode implies 'w' and
4390 | |     raises an `FileExistsError` if the file already exists.
4391 | |
4392 | |     Python distinguishes between files opened in binary and text modes,
4393 | |     even when the underlying operating system doesn't.  Files opened in
4394 | |     binary mode (appending 'b' to the mode argument) return contents as
4395 | |     bytes objects without any decoding.  In text mode (the default, or when
4396 | |     't' is appended to the mode argument), the contents of the file are
4397 | |     returned as strings, the bytes having been first decoded using a
4398 | |     platform-dependent encoding or using the specified encoding if given.
4399 | |
4400 | |     buffering is an optional integer used to set the buffering policy.
4401 | |     Pass 0 to switch buffering off (only allowed in binary mode), 1 to
4402 | |     select line buffering (only usable in text mode), and an integer > 1 to
4403 | |     indicate the size of a fixed-size chunk buffer.   When no buffering
4404 | |     argument is given, the default buffering policy works as follows:
4405 | |
4406 | |     * Binary files are buffered in fixed-size chunks; the size of the buffer
4407 | |       is max(min(blocksize, 8 MiB), DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE) when the device
4408 | |       block size is available.
4409 | |       On most systems, the buffer will typically be 128 kilobytes long.
4410 | |
4411 | |     * "Interactive" text files (files for which isatty() returns True)
4412 | |       use line buffering.  Other text files use the policy described above
4413 | |       for binary files.
4414 | |
4415 | |     encoding is the name of the encoding used to decode or encode the
4416 | |     file.  This should only be used in text mode.  The default encoding is
4417 | |     platform dependent, but any encoding supported by Python can be
4418 | |     passed.  See the codecs module for the list of supported encodings.
4419 | |
4420 | |     errors is an optional string that specifies how encoding errors are to
4421 | |     be handled---this argument should not be used in binary mode.  Pass
4422 | |     'strict' to raise a ValueError exception if there is an encoding error
4423 | |     (the default of None has the same effect), or pass 'ignore' to ignore
4424 | |     errors.  (Note that ignoring encoding errors can lead to data loss.)
4425 | |     See the documentation for codecs.register or run 'help(codecs.Codec)'
4426 | |     for a list of the permitted encoding error strings.
4427 | |
4428 | |     newline controls how universal newlines works (it only applies to text
4429 | |     mode).  It can be None, '', '\\n', '\\r', and '\\r\\n'.  It works as
4430 | |     follows:
4431 | |
4432 | |     * On input, if newline is None, universal newlines mode is enabled.
4433 | |       Lines in the input can end in '\\n', '\\r', or '\\r\\n', and these are
4434 | |       translated into '\\n' before being returned to the caller.  If it is
4435 | |       '', universal newline mode is enabled, but line endings are returned
4436 | |       to the caller untranslated.  If it has any of the other legal values,
4437 | |       input lines are only terminated by the given string, and the line
4438 | |       ending is returned to the caller untranslated.
4439 | |
4440 | |     * On output, if newline is None, any '\\n' characters written are
4441 | |       translated to the system default line separator, os.linesep.  If
4442 | |       newline is '' or '\\n', no translation takes place.  If newline is any
4443 | |       of the other legal values, any '\\n' characters written are translated
4444 | |       to the given string.
4445 | |
4446 | |     If closefd is False, the underlying file descriptor will be kept open
4447 | |     when the file is closed.  This does not work when a file name is given
4448 | |     and must be True in that case.
4449 | |
4450 | |     A custom opener can be used by passing a callable as *opener*.  The
4451 | |     underlying file descriptor for the file object is then obtained by
4452 | |     calling *opener* with (*file*, *flags*).  *opener* must return an open
4453 | |     file descriptor (passing os.open as *opener* results in functionality
4454 | |     similar to passing None).
4455 | |
4456 | |     open() returns a file object whose type depends on the mode, and
4457 | |     through which the standard file operations such as reading and writing
4458 | |     are performed.  When open() is used to open a file in a text mode ('w',
4459 | |     'r', 'wt', 'rt', etc.), it returns a TextIOWrapper.  When used to open
4460 | |     a file in a binary mode, the returned class varies: in read binary
4461 | |     mode, it returns a BufferedReader; in write binary and append binary
4462 | |     modes, it returns a BufferedWriter, and in read/write mode, it returns
4463 | |     a BufferedRandom.
